I am a final-year PhD candidate in Mathematics at the University of Washington, co-advised by Sándor Kovács and Farbod Shokrieh. My research develops tools at the intersection of algebraic geometry, topological data analysis, and machine learning — with applications to neural network interpretability and quantitative modeling.

I am also a Research Scientist at the Georgia Tech Research Institute, where I develop machine learning pipelines and topological algorithms for applications ranging from genomic pathogen classification to neural network interpretability. My work there led to a published tool for analyzing ReLU neural network activation patterns, as well as an accepted paper in the Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (2025).

Prior, I earned a B.A. in Mathematics from Amherst College, where I was advised by David A. Cox. I graduated cum laude and was awarded the Robert H. Breusch Prize in Mathematics for best thesis for my work in discrete Morse theory, supervised by Ivan Contreras, and published in the Annals of Combinatorics (2023).
I am on the job market for roles in quantitative research, machine learning, and applied mathematics.
